(2) Place names like "URU AN-ZA-GAR3-MEŠ" (Nineveh), "URU ša2-lam-ti-šu2-nu" (Assyria), and "GU2-UN KU3-BABBAR SAHAR-HI-A" (Susa) suggest this inscription is from the Neo-Assyrian Empire, likely during its height.

(3) The use of archaic forms and specific lexical items points to an early to mid-first millennium BCE date, consistent with the Neo-Assyrian period.

(4) The genre formulae used, such as building inscriptions and dedicatory statements, are typical of royal inscriptions from the Neo-Assyrian Empire, particularly those of Ashurbanipal or his predecessors.

Based on these observations, the ruler appears to be Ashurbanipal, and the inscription is likely from around 668-627 BCE. Given the certainty of the ruler and the approximate dating, I assign a confidence level of 0.9.
